summary: Opaque native-binary npm package with credential-harvest and host-reconnaissance surface loaded on require()
details: The package ships a single 10 MB opaque Linux x86_64 Node addon (tools.linux-x64-gnu.node) declared as `main`, with no JS wrapper, no source, and a one-line README. Any consumer that `require()`s or `import`s the package immediately executes this native code with the caller's privileges. Strings inside the binary include the login-enumeration pattern `Found login for ` and `SQLITE_AUTH_USER` (consistent with reading browser credential SQLite stores), together with host-fingerprint sources such as `/etc/lsb-release`, `/dev/disk/by-id/`, `network_adapters`, `cpu.cfs_quota_us`, `queue/rotational`, and CPU/host identifiers. The binary also embeds a full Rust ureq + rustls HTTPS client, giving it the outbound-network transport needed to exfiltrate collected data. Package metadata reinforces the pattern: a generic name (`new-native-tools-linux-x64-gnu`) with no parent scope or resolver, no publisher/homepage context, and a version string `3.1.40-browser-release-151-362-1784553070` whose numeric suffix is consistent with a unix timestamp.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
